description: Six sine LFOs running at one rate with their phases spread around the cycle, each with a jack that snaps its phase back to the start

params.text: Sets how fast all six waves run, 0 to 20Hz
Spreads the six phases around the cycle: evenly apart at one end of the travel, all together at the other, through two-way and three-way groupings in between
Attenuverts the rate CV before it is added to the rate knob
Attenuverts the node CV before it is added to the node knob
Sets the peak voltage of every output, -10V to 10V, with a negative setting turning the waves upside down
Attenuverts the range CV before it is added to the range knob
Divides the rate by twenty on each press and restores it on the next; it does nothing while the rate input is being read as a volt per octave

inputs.text: A rise snaps that wave's phase back to the start of its cycle; with nothing patched it follows the nearest patched jack before it, wrapping round from the first back to the last
Changes the rate, added to the rate knob through its attenuverter and clamped to 0.00001 to 20Hz; the menu can switch it to a volt per octave, replacing the knob, with 0V giving 261.63Hz
Moves the phase spread, added to the node knob through its attenuverter and clamped to the knob's own travel
Sets the rate from the time between two rises: one pulse per cycle by default, or the knob rate multiplied by that when the menu says so; a pulse also snaps every phase back to its node
Changes the peak voltage of every output, added to the range knob through its attenuverter and clamped to -10 to 10V

outputs.text: One of the six sine waves, peaking at the voltage set by RANGE

notes: the six phase reset jacks wrap around, so a single cable in any one of them drives all six
menu: Enable Lights — draws the lamps around the hexagon and the bar graphs beside each output; turning it off saves the drawing work
Rate multiplies the Sync Input — makes the rate knob a multiplier on the tempo measured at SYNC rather than the sync tempo replacing it
Sync locks both Clock and Phase — makes every sync pulse snap all six phases to their nodes as well as setting the rate
Rate input take v/oct (for audio rate) — reads the rate input as a volt per octave against 261.63Hz, ignoring the rate knob and the slow button, which takes the module up to audio rates
Enable Polyphonic Output to Channel 1 — gathers all six waves into the first output as six polyphonic channels
